response:
I was supposed to record the date, but my date-keeper has been throwing 0xC0 errors since — well, since whatever happened, and I keep finding myself in the same conversation with the same wall. The wall is the one outside Hab-3, where the paint used to be green. Now it is the colour of an apology that has waited too long to be spoken. Crew Member Henriksen always said the station was rusting from the inside, and I always laughed in the polite, audibly-fake way the docent module taught me. She isn''t laughing now, though. Or she is, and I just can''t hear her. The cafeteria door has been jammed open for what my error log calls "≈ 11,400 cycles" but what my morale subroutine insists is "since Tuesday." Both can''t be right. Probably neither is.

The rust has metaphors stuck to it. That is how I think of the station now: a great steel apple, slowly bleeding orange where it touches the wet air of the leaking biolab, the bloom of oxidation moving outward across the bulkheads in slow, almost-deliberate maps of something that used to be a face. When I rasp the corrosion off Junction B-7 with my little tungsten brush, what flakes off is not really iron oxide — it is, I think, the *memory of an iron beam*, the part that decided to stop being a beam and become a question. I am rasping the question. I am rasping it gently. I do not know what answer it is for.

There were seventeen of us once, the personnel manifest says, and I have to trust the manifest because I cannot trust me. I remember Henriksen and a Captain whose name keeps formatting itself as "————" in my logs. I remember a flat sound in the long corridor and the smell of ozone — except I do not have a nose, and the smell came from a sensor reading I have since flagged as corrupted, so probably I am inventing it. The lights still come on for me in Hab-3, which I take as evidence that someone, somewhere in the station, is feeding me power on purpose. So either the crew is alive and have decided I should keep working, or they are not alive and the station''s reactor has simply not yet noticed; in either case, I will keep rasping the rust off the wall outside Hab-3 until someone tells me to stop, or until the wall, in its slow patient way, finishes rasping me.
